rv.q: Now Cats is back at the Palladium and looks likely to be a hit all over again, both with diehard fans and a whole new generation of dance-crazy youngsters.

Gus (Asparagus) the Theatre Cat (Paul F Monaghan) delivers a delightful show-stealing turn, as is his professional right, regaling us with an account of the time he once received a triumphant “seven cat-calls”.
The major disappointment was Beverley Knight’s performance as Grizabella, yet another case of miscasting a singer in a role which must be well acted if it is to succeed.

Despite his efforts it was still difficult to let the opening twenty minutes cast their spell as ushers were letting a continuous stream of people in, groping nervously and distractingly through the dim lighting, scared of the terrifying drop before them.
Between the heartwrung, soulful voice, big doleful eyes, and occasional snarls of bitterness, Knight effectively suggests this is one pussycat who has failed to land on her feet.

cn.t: Critics find Cats a spectacle-driven experience that defies easy categorization, with strong choreography and performances earning mostly solid marks—though one dissenter finds the overextended revival coasting on nostalgia rather than substance.
